findings.description: W1 THE t100 STUB'S EXECUTION NARRATIVE DOES NOT MATCH THE ACTUAL GENERATOR; THE SUBSTANCE IS VERIFIED BUT GROOM MUST RE-FENCE FROM ITS OWN MEASUREMENT, NOT FROM THE STUB'S STRINGS. Review independently read backend/scripts/docs_verification.py and the committed report: the committed docs/criteria/docs_verification.md is 54 lines (git show HEAD agrees), not the stub's '190 lines', and the stub's claimed run narrative - '189 lines', header 'VERIFICATION REPORT / Base SHA / Head SHA / Node: v24.16.0', and check names 'INDEX-ANCHORS: PASS 4/4', 'STORED-GATES: PASS 4/4', 'INDEX-ENTROPY', 'STALE-REFS', 'npx tsc --noEmit', 'npx jest --ci', 'python -m pytest' - describes none of what this generator emits (grep: no Base SHA / tsc / jest / pytest / ENTROPY / STALE-REFS strings anywhere in the tracked tree outside t100's own card; the real tokens are 'INDEX_ANCHORS PASS floor=256 entries=318' at line 381 and 'STORED_GATES PASS executed=9 failures=0 restored=1'; INDEX_ANCHORS has EIGHT keys {16,54,131,132,133,135,215,216}, not 'keys 131,132,133,135'). The load-bearing facts DO all verify: line 46 is exactly the 133: ("t26", 6e9723e8...) literal; the other seven anchors match their stored entry_sha; the report footer is CHECKS_FAILED 1; the footer recipe 'ALL_CHECKS_PASS if not FAILS else CHECKS_FAILED n' is at line 500 exactly as AC2 states; docs_verification.py carries exactly 13 64-hex literals and a single-value replacement preserves 13 (leg 258's HEX=13 leg is safe). REMEDY (mandatory at groom t100): every fenced expectation string is taken from groom's own re-run of the generator, never from the stub's narrative; an AC2 fenced verbatim from the stub ('INDEX-ANCHORS: PASS 4/4') would false-RED a correct build. This is a warning not an error because the stub itself hard-rules 'groom re-measures, does not inherit', and the card's verification discipline section repeats it.

W2 t100's ALL_CHECKS_PASS REQUIREMENT IS POLLUTION-SENSITIVE AND THE BOUNDARY FIX LANDS DOWNSTREAM OF IT - THE CLEAN-RUN CONDITION IS A REAL SCHEDULING OBLIGATION, NOT ADVISORY. t100's AC2/AC3 require the generator to run rc=0 with an ALL_CHECKS_PASS footer and the committed report regenerated from that run, but the SKIP_DIRS build/+scratch/ exclusion is t102, which by the single-writer rule must land AFTER t100. Review measured the current main checkout with the generator's own walk semantics: 2117 *.md visible under the current SKIP_DIRS vs 266 with build+scratch excluded (265 tracked) - i.e. running the generator naively on the working checkout today produces exactly the survey-reproduced LINK_CHECK FAIL broken=N class (t102's own Measured base state records the survey hit it: broken=14, footer 1->3, and restored the report with git checkout). If t100's builder regenerates from a polluted tree, AC2 fails through pollution, or worse, a polluted report gets committed and leg 258 (the leg this card exists to recover) stays RED for the wrong reason. REMEDY at groom t100: fence the regeneration leg with an explicit pre-run pollution gate (assert no build/ or scratch/ payload visible to the walk, or run the generator against a clean git-archive extraction and copy the byte-identical clean output in), and assert the committed report's LINK_CHECK line matches the clean-tree count. Recorded as a warning because the mechanism is disclosed in t102's stub and the fix is a fencing obligation, not a design defect.

W3 SMALL COUNT ERRORS IN THE STUBS ARE ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT AND MUST NOT BE FENCED AS ABSOLUTE NUMBERS. (a) t102 AC1 says SKIP_DIRS gains build/scratch 'in addition to the nine existing members' - the set at line 96 has SIX members (.git, node_modules, .venv, __pycache__, dist, staging). (b) t102's walk-size story (2116 visible / 265 excluded / 261 tracked) re-measured at review HEAD as 2117 / 266 / 265 - the +1 is the same 4-new-cards effect the stub describes, now committed, and the whole figure drifts with every scratch payload. (c) t101's '2863 *.md visible to leg 214's walk' re-measured at review as 2173 under the same .git/node_modules-only skip - again scratch-drift, same order of conclusion. None of these numbers is load-bearing: t102's actual deliverable is the INVARIANCE (report byte-identical with and without the two directories present, measured both ways) and t101's is the rc=0-on-clean + bites-on-dirt pair. Groom must fence invariances and rc outcomes, and where a count is fenced (e.g. files=) it must be derived in the same leg, never copied from a stub. warn-also: t99's stub statement that the committed report is '190 lines' does not exist in that form (the 190 figure is t100's; t99 only says the report still ends CHECKS_FAILED, which is true).

W4 THE t99 NEGATIVE CONTROL MUST ASSERT THE NAMED PIN LINE, NOT JUST rc!=0, BECAUSE THE AMENDED LEGS CAN GO RED FOR OTHER REASONS. Review verified the amendment arithmetic independently and it is exact: the stale 6e9723e8 literal occurs exactly twice in the 318-entry index (tests[190], tests[191]); tests[133]'s current entry_sha is 09cb7d9a...; the single 64-char substitution is length-preserving (3610->3610, 4167->4167); and all four before/after command-sha and entry_sha pairs in the stub recompute to the stub's values under the binding recipe sha256(json.dumps(entry,separators=(',',':'))). But the pin loop is not a pure digest check: for(const n of [131,132,133,135]) also execSync's each pinned leg's command, so a perturbed-tests[133] run can RED on either the digest comparison or the re-executed command, and legs 190/191 are already RED today on their own unrelated premises (freeze-scope drift / README drifted). AC3's 'still RED when tests[133] is perturbed' is therefore only a real negative control if the fenced assertion matches the specific stderr line 'ac3 RED: byte-pin entry 133 changed' (and AC4's positive control likewise asserts the ABSENCE of that line while recording the other RED lines verbatim - which the stub already requires). Also note the stored legs read the index from disk via fs.readFileSync, so the 'in memory' perturbation of AC3 must be done on a scratch copy of the index with the leg replayed against it (the stub's Measured-base-state section already uses scratch copies; groom must fence the same path). Warning only: the AC intent is right, the fencing detail is groom's.

W5 NO GAPS AGAINST OPERATOR-AUTHORIZED SCOPE (WAL 1201); FOUR DELIBERATE NON-COVERAGES RECORDED SO GROOM DOES NOT ABSORB THEM. Authorized workstream A (anchor[133] refresh) is fully owned: index side t99, generator side t100, ordering t99->t100 so the index stops asserting the stale digest before the generator does. Authorized workstream B is fully owned: B1 (leg-214 gate matrix) + B3 (leg-255 stale as-stored pin) in t101 as one fence-artifact premise correction, B2 (sweep-runner node_modules allowlist) in t102 as the pollution-boundary deliverable. Nothing unauthorized crept in: no feature, no endpoint, no dependency, no new REQ-ID, no closed-card/WAL touch, and the survey's own new disclosure (making scratch/ gitignored) is explicitly pushed OUT of t102 to an operator decision. The four deliberate non-coverages, each stated in-card rather than silently dropped: (1) leg 214's stored command is NOT patched (index-owned; t101 records the boundary, t102 records the obligation); (2) the orchestrator-side sweep runner is not a repo artifact - t102 AC4(c) ships the allowlist discipline as a WAL housekeeping obligation with the required exclusion set; (3) the WSL-node/jsdom environment class is disclosed and routed to canonical-host discipline, never fixed as a product change; (4) t95's closed card/handoff bytes are never edited - the correction lands by reference. The t101 B1+B3 merge is sound per the t96 {232,250} coordinated-set precedent (one artifact, two premises, per-defect record entries and separate ACs preserve per-defect rigor) and matches the operator's split-finer instruction, which the split honors by separating the genuinely different deliverable classes (index record / generator edit / premise record / verifier+policy).

W6 MILESTONE BOOKKEEPING: THIS REVIEW APPLIED STEP 6 ITSELF (DEVIATION FROM THE phase_14 W9 PRECEDENT, DISCLOSED). skills/definer/details/review_plan.md Step 6 and the mode's Boundaries allow writing docs/state/milestones/phase_15_gate_amendments.json, and this run's task instruction explicitly permits setting review_plan_status; unlike the phase_14 run, no single-writer constraint blocked the milestone file. It has therefore been updated in-place by this review: review_plan_status in_progress -> passed, review_plan_completed_at set, review_plan_verdict PASS_WITH_WARNINGS, review_plan_attempts 0 -> 1, and it is committed alongside this handoff on main. The orchestrator should VERIFY (not re-apply) the values, mirror them into its own state and the WAL, and note that the schema enum for this handoff is the PASS/PASS_WITH_WARNINGS/FAIL verdict while the milestone file's status field carries the lifecycle value 'passed' - the phase_14 file used the same shape. No card, plan, dag.json, backlog, or issue_map edit is required or made by this review.

checks.coverage_check: complete - the two operator-authorized workstreams (WAL 1201) map 1:1 onto the four cards: A anchor[133] -> t99 (index tests[190]/[191] byte-pins) + t100 (generator INDEX_ANCHORS[133] + report regeneration); B1 leg-214 matrix + B3 leg-255 stale pin -> t101 (one t95-fence premise-correction record, t96 coordinated-set precedent); B2 sweep-runner allowlist -> t102 (SKIP_DIRS build+scratch in-repo + recorded orchestrator-side allowlist obligation). Every authorized item is owned by exactly one card; no card owns anything outside the authorization (plan phase_15 section, backlog rows 104-107, issue_map t99-t102 -> 105-108, milestone issues_generated, and all four card frontmatters agree). See W5 for the four stated non-coverages.
checks.granularity_check: complete - config limits.issue_granularity max_acs=6 max_files=4 max_diff_lines=300 warn_only=true. Survey-stage cards carry 6 AC drafts each (t99 6, t100 6, t101 6, t102 6) within max_acs; authored file sets are t99 1 (record) + card + handoff, t100 2 (generator + regenerated report), t101 1 (record), t102 3 (generator + report + record) - all within max_files; diff lines are single-literal/single-line code edits plus record bodies, well inside 300 on the code side and the record-body convention is the operator-approved t89/t90/t94/t96 amendment-record shape. The split was evaluated against the operator's split-finer instruction and is rigorous BY DELIVERABLE MECHANISM: the anchor debt is correctly TWO cards (index record vs generator code, different files, different delivery, different baseline effects) and not finer (each half is one literal substitution); B1+B3 are one closed artifact's two premises (splitting would force two ac_hash passes over one closed artifact for zero observability gain); B2 is a third deliverable class. Cyclic reasoning check: none - each card is single-mechanism with exactly one predicted baseline effect (t99 ZERO, t100 33->32, t101 ZERO, t102 ZERO).
checks.dependency_check: complete - dag.json parsed programmatically: 103 nodes, 144 edges, cycles field [], independent DFS cycle check found 0 cycles, no duplicate edges, no edge endpoint missing from nodes, topological_order covers all 103 nodes with 0 child-before-parent violations under the child->parent edge convention (t99 pos 99 < t100 pos 100 < t102 pos 102). The ONLY new edges are (t100,t99) and (t102,t100) and they match the card frontmatter depends EXACTLY: t99 [], t100 [t99], t101 [], t102 [t100]. The single-writer rule on docs_verification.py + docs/criteria/docs_verification.md (t100, t102) is therefore enforced IN THE DAG, not merely in prose - the phase_14 W1 weakness is structurally closed here. t101 is a true independent root (0 in-edges, 0 out-edges) and file-disjoint from the chain (record-only; touches neither the generator, the report, nor the index), so it is safe in the parallel slot beside the chain head; its orphan status is the legitimate independent-root class (like t96/t97 were), distinct from the pre-existing t72/t73/t74/t96/t97 zero-edge orphans reviewed in earlier milestones. Critical path t99->t100->t102 agrees with the dag.json critical_path field.
checks.duplicate_contradiction_check: complete - no two cards share an identical AC; no contradictory AC found. The shared-surface rules are mutually consistent: t100 and t102 both name the single-writer rule and agree t102 lands after t100; t101 and t102 both address pollution but at different layers (t101 corrects EXPECTATIONS, t102 hardens the in-repo WALK and records the boundary) and t102's AC4(a) references t101's corrected 214 premise rather than restating it differently; every card's constraint list agrees that the index is orchestrator-owned and that 214's stored command is NOT patched by any card; the frozen-33 set is byte-identical in all four cards and its membership was verified against the index (190, 191, 258, 259, 227, 231 are members; 214, 217, 255 are not; the set counts 33). The t95 non-rewrite rule (t101) and the record-only delivery rule (t99) reinforce rather than conflict.
checks.re_premise_direction_check: complete for every re-premise in the milestone, and each was independently re-derived from the shipped index where it is a digest claim: tests[190]/[191] (stale 6e9723e8 -> as-shipped 09cb7d9a, single length-preserving substitution, all four before/after command-sha/entry_sha pairs RECOMPUTED CORRECT at review, negative control = perturbed 133 re-fires the pin, see W4 for the fencing nuance); generator INDEX_ANCHORS[133] (same re-premise on the generator side, negative control = revert re-fires the anchor FAIL, and the 13-hex-literal count is preserved so leg 258's HEX leg is untouched); t95 ac5 expectation (214 premised RED -> GREEN-on-clean with the dirt negative control EXECUTED in a throwaway tree so the leg is proven still to bite - re-premise, not dismissal); t95 ac6 pin table (9aac9f0c/487b30e2/7945 superseded by the shipped f5aafe07/1878e29d/7760 - review recomputed both digests from the shipped tests[255] entry and the stub's triple is EXACTLY right, and the 9aac9f0c literal appears nowhere in the index); SKIP_DIRS (boundary exclusion with a tracked-doc broken-link negative control so the gate can still fail). No card deletes protection to make a gate green; every card states RE-PREMISE-never-relax as a FAIL condition, and every negative control is required to be EXECUTED, not asserted.
checks.measurement_provenance_check: complete with the W1/W3 exceptions itemized - review re-measured read-only (no gates executed, no repo writes beyond the two allowed files): index has 318 entries; 6e9723e8 occurs exactly twice (legs 190, 191, both t47); tests[133] entry_sha 09cb7d9a..., command sha b2a662b9..., length 3547; legs 190/191 lengths 3610/4167 and all four before/after digest pairs recompute; 255's shipped triple f5aafe07/1878e29d/7760 recomputes exactly; leg 259's a77f98a0 index-byte pin and '-eq 259' leg exist verbatim and 81f05126 appears nowhere in 259 (the stub's correction of the earlier belief is right); no leg other than 190/191 embeds any current entry_sha of {133,190,191,204,216} at prefix 64/40/20/12; leg 258's ALL_CHECKS_PASS / ENT>=256 / HEX=13 premises confirmed present and HEX=13 confirmed on the file; leg 214's walk skips only node_modules/.git; .gitignore:185 build/ present and no scratch entry; .env absent from the checkout; SKIP_DIRS at line 96 has six members; frozen-33 membership spot-checked. The stub values that did NOT re-measure are exactly those in W1 (t100's narrative strings) and W3 (walk counts, the 'nine members' phrase) - all covered by the cards' own groom-re-measures hard rule. This review executed no gates and made no claims beyond the reads above.

evidence.notes: Verdict rationale: zero errors, six warnings (W1-W6). The plan's core arithmetic - the digest pairs, the frozen-33 baseline, the 33->32 prediction surface (258 recovers, 259 stays RED on its two named unsatisfiable premises), the ZERO-delta claims for t99/t101/t102, and the DAG shape - survived independent recomputation. The warnings are groom-fencing obligations (W1 strings, W2 clean-run gate, W3 derived-counts-only, W4 named-line control) plus scope/bookkeeping disclosures (W5, W6). Groom order must follow the DAG; t101 may run in parallel with t99/t100.
